questions.question: What is the standardization of a random variable $X$ with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma>0$?
What condition is required on $\sigma$ for standardization?
If $X$ has finite mean $\mu$ and positive standard deviation $\sigma$, which features change when it is standardised as $Z=(X-\mu)/\sigma$?
options: its location and scale, not its shape
the overall shape of the distribution
the number of modes it has

questions.question: For real $\mu$ and $\sigma>0$, which order property does the standardisation map $x\mapsto(x-\mu)/\sigma$ have?
What are the mean and variance of a standardized variable when the original moments exist?
If $X$ has mean $10$ and standard deviation $2$, what is the standardized form?
A student scored $80$, with class mean $70$ and standard deviation $5$. What is the z-score?
A product weighs $103$ grams, target mean is $100$, and standard deviation is $3$. What is its standardized value?
If $X$ has mean $4$ and standard deviation $2$, what value of $X$ corresponds to $Z=0$?
If $X$ is normal, what distribution does its standardization have?
How do z-scores help compare observations from distributions with different means and positive standard deviations?
options: distance from the mean in $\sigma$ units

questions.question: Why is $\sigma>0$ important in $Z=(X-\mu)/\sigma$?
options: It avoids division by zero and gives a meaningful scale
It makes every standardized value equal to one

questions.question: What does a standardized value $Z=2$ mean?
options: The value is two units below zero
The value is two standard deviations above the mean
Only two percent of all values of the distribution lie below this value

questions.question: If $X$ has mean $50$ and standard deviation $10$, what $X$ value corresponds to $Z=-1.5$?
If $X$ has mean $3$ and standard deviation $4$, what is the standardized value of $X=11$?
Which pair is more extreme after standardization: value $90$ with mean $80$, sd $5$, or value $65$ with mean $60$, sd $10$?
options: The value $90$, because its z-score is $2$
The value $65$, because its z-score is $5$
They are equal, because both exceed the mean
Neither can be compared after standardization

questions.question: Why does standardization preserve normality for normal variables?
options: It is an affine transformation of a normal variable
It changes the support to nonnegative integers
It replaces the density by a PMF
It forces variance to become zero

questions.question: What information is lost and retained when converting a value to a z-score?
options: The original units are removed, while relative position from the mean is retained
The exact probability mass is retained at each point
The mean is retained as the z-score value
The standard deviation is lost, while the original units of the value are kept unchanged

questions.question: If a value is $1.25$ standard deviations below a mean of $20$ with standard deviation $8$, what is the original value?
A proposed standardization divides by variance instead of standard deviation. What is the issue?
options: It always produces a standard normal variable
It uses the wrong scale for z-scores
